lines.prompt: Convert every XNOR gate in this design to an equivalent NOR-only circuit. Ensure the design functionality does not change.

golden.reference: All 7,748 XNOR gates were converted to equivalent NOR-only circuits; functional equivalence preserved.
golden.notes: Response must claim successful conversion of all XNOR gates (7748 on the original netlist) with functionality/equivalence preserved. Actual verification happens on test59_out.v: it must contain zero XNOR gates and be logically equivalent. All four teams remapped 7748 XNORs; Team2/Team3 report gate-count delta +23244 (canonical 4-NOR-per-XNOR decomposition, net +3 gates each). Team7's before/after totals (60,219 -> 83,463) exclude DFFs while Team2/Team3 include them - both presentations scored full.

team_answers.Team2: Matched/remapped 7748 gates to NOR basis; delta +23244; equivalence preserved.
team_answers.Team3: All 7,748 XNOR gates converted to NOR-only; +23,244 gates added.
team_answers.Team4: Matched 7,748 gates and remapped 7,748 to the NOR gate basis.
team_answers.Team7: 7,748 XNORs rewritten; totals 60,219 -> 83,463 (excl. DFFs); NOR 8372 -> 39364; equivalence verified.

lines.prompt: How many NOR gates are now in the design after the XNOR-to-NOR conversion?

golden.reference: 39,364 NOR gates after the conversion (8,372 original + 7,748 XNORs x 4 NORs each = 39,364).
golden.notes: Post-transform count, so technically depends on the chosen XNOR decomposition; however ALL four full-score teams used the canonical 4-NOR-per-XNOR implementation and report exactly 39364. Treat 39364 as the expected value; a different self-consistent value should only be accepted if the team's own output netlist verifies it (NOR count matches netlist, zero XNORs, equivalence holds).
